references.text: The children of Israel cried out to the Lord in distress, and he raised up a deliverer for them - a recurring pattern in the book of Judges
The children of Israel cried out to the Lord because of the Midianites - the same expression for prayer in distress
The people confess their sin with similar words: 'We have sinned because we have forsaken the Lord and worshiped the Baals'
Samuel urges the people to remove foreign gods and the Baals and turn back to the Lord
Joshua warns the people against forsaking the Lord to serve foreign gods
The children of Israel groaned and cried out to God under slavery in Egypt - a fundamental pattern for crying out to the Lord in distress
Elijah confronts the people about wavering between the Lord and Baal - the same conflict with Baal worship
Nehemiah summarizes Israel's history with repeated sin, crying out to God, and God's deliverance through judges
